subject: chemistry
question_text: Assign oxidation numbers to the underlined elements in each of the following species: (a) K₂MnO₄ (manganese) (b) H₂S₂O₇ (sulphur).

verification.note: Chapter 5 (Stoichiometry) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.66-72), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. The book underlines Mn and S; underlining cannot be reproduced here, so the elements are named in brackets instead. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. This chapter has NO Long Answer section in the book, so no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. AI chemistry check 2026-08-25 (audit round): step s2 jumped from 2x = +12 straight to the box, so a student copying the model answer committed the exact error the step's own common_mistakes warns about. The line 'x = +6, so each S in H₂S₂O₇ is +6' was added to the marked lines; marks and mark split unchanged.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Mn in K₂MnO₄
lines: Let the oxidation number of Mn be x.
x = +6, so Mn in K₂MnO₄ is +6
steps.why: Potassium and oxygen have fixed rule values, so the sum rule for a neutral compound gives one equation in x.
common_mistakes: Reporting +7 from memory of KMnO₄. K₂MnO₄ (manganate) is a different compound: Mn is +6 here.
Counting one K instead of two.
steps.memory_tip: One K means permanganate and +7; two K means manganate and +6.
steps.margin_note: The full equation with x = +6 earns this mark.

steps.label: S in H₂S₂O₇
lines: Let the oxidation number of S be x.
x = +6, so each S in H₂S₂O₇ is +6

lines.text: Mn in K₂MnO₄ = +6 ;  S in H₂S₂O₇ = +6

steps.why: The same sum rule applies; here two sulphur atoms share 2x, so 2x = 12 must be halved to +6 for one atom.
common_mistakes: Reporting +12 for sulphur without dividing by the two S atoms.
steps.memory_tip: H₂S₂O₇ is two H₂SO₄ units minus one water — sulphur stays at +6, the same as in sulphuric acid.
steps.margin_note: Divide 2x by 2 on its own line, then box both results, each with its + sign.

insider_note: Part (a) is a deliberate trap beside KMnO₄: the extra potassium drops manganese from +7 to +6, and quoting +7 from memory is the common lost mark.
